questions.question: Identify the odd option in relation to the oceanic layers.
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is **The Oceanic Slope.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Scientists have divided the ocean into **five main layers**. These layers, known as "zones", extend from the surface to the most extreme depths.

 
 
• **Epipelagic Zone** - It extends from the surface to 200 meters (656 feet).
 
• **Mesopelagic Zone** - Below the epipelagic zone is the mesopelagic zone, extending from 200 meters (656 feet) to 1,000 meters (3,281 feet).
 
• **Bathypelagic Zone** - This zone extends from 1,000 meters (3,281 feet) down to 4,000 meters (13,124 feet).
 
• **Abyssopelagic Zone** - It extends from 4,000 meters (13,124 feet) to 6,000 meters (19,686 feet).
 
• **Hadalpelagic Zone** - This layer extends from 6,000 meters (19,686 feet) to the bottom of the deepest parts of the ocean.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b64361ee292c0fcd7b63724865a9a9859546faee709aa5e4f599110edd4bb52f.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The ocean deeps** are the deepest part of the ocean. They are long, narrow, steep-sided and flat-floored depressions on the ocean floor.
 
• A **continental shelf **is a portion of a continent that is submerged under an area of relatively shallow water known as a shelf sea. 
 
• The continuously sloping portion of the continental margin, seaward of the continental shelf and extending down to the deep sea floor of the abyssal plain, is known as** the continental slope**. It is characterised by gradients of 2.5 degrees. It extends between the depth of 180 to 3600 metres.

questions.question: Who is the 50th Chief Justice of India?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**DY Chandrachud**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• **Dhananjaya Yeshwant Chandrachud**

 
 
• He currently holds the position of the 50th Chief Justice of India, serving since **November 2022 to 10 November 2024**.
 
• Justice Chandrachud has been involved in several landmark judgments, shaping the legal landscape of India.
 
• Electoral Bond Scheme Verdict,Ram Janmabhoomi Verdict, Privacy Verdict, Decriminalization of Homosexuality, Sabarimala Case, Revocation of Jammu and Kashmir's Special Status.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Supreme Court of India is the **highest judicial court and the final court of appeal** under the Constitution of India, the highest constitutional court, with the power of judicial review.
 
• India is a federal State and has a single and unified judicial system with **three tier structure, i.e. Supreme Court, High Courts and Subordinate Courts**.The promulgation of **Regulating Act of 1773** established the Supreme Court of Judicature at Calcutta as a Court of Record, with full power & authority.
 
• The Federal Court had jurisdiction to solve disputes between provinces and federal states and hear **appeal against Judgements from High Courts**.
 
• After India attained independence in 1947, the Constitution of India came into being on 26 January 1950. The Supreme Court of India also came into existence and its first sitting was held on **28 January 1950**.
 
• The Indian constitution provides for a provision of Supreme Court under** Part V (The Union)** and Chapter 6 (The Union Judiciary).
 
• **Articles 124 to 147 in Part V** of the Constitution deal with the organisation, independence, jurisdiction, powers and procedures of the Supreme Court.
 
• The Indian constitution under **Article 124(1)** states that there shall be a Supreme Court of India constituting of a Chief Justice of India (CJI) and, until Parliament by law prescribes a larger number, of not more than seven other Judges.
 
• Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Bill of 2019 has added four judges to strength. It increased the judicial strength **from 31 to 34**, including the CJI.

questions.question: Identify the type of cell that is long and branched.
questions.solution:
The correct solution is __**Nerve cell.**__

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• Nerve cells, or neurons, are fundamental components of the **nervous system**.
 
• It transmits electrical impulses and facilitates communication within the body.
 
• Nerve cells, or neurons, have a distinctive structure with a cell body,
 
 
• **Dendrites **(which receive signals), and
 
• **Axon** (which transmits signals). 
 
 
 
• **Neurotransmitters**, chemical messengers, are released at the synapses (junctions) between neurons—to transmit signals from one neuron to another.
 
• Nerve cells have various functions, including sensory processing, motor control, cognitive functions like memory and learning, and regulating bodily functions like heart rate and digestion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__ **

 
• Blood cells are essential components of the **circulatory system**, responsible for various functions crucial to maintaining health and well-being.
 
• There are three main types of blood cells:
 
 
• **Red blood cells (erythrocytes), **
 
• **White blood cells (leukocytes), and **
 
• **Platelets (thrombocytes).** 
 
 
 
• **Red Blood Cells (RBCs):** Red blood cells are responsible for carrying oxygen from the lungs to tissues throughout the body and transporting carbon dioxide back to the lungs for exhalation. They contain **hemoglobin**,a protein that binds to oxygen molecules.
 
• **White Blood Cells (WBCs):** White blood cells are part of the immune system and play a crucial role in defending the body **against infections** and foreign invaders. 
 
• **Platelets:** Platelets are small cell fragments involved in **blood clotting (coagulation)**. When a blood vessel is injured, platelets adhere to the site of injury and release clotting factors to form a blood clot, which helps prevent excessive bleeding. Platelets also participate in wound healing and tissue repair processes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/89852d4a58e7a84f229f9238d8dcad12539fa2ab4c538083c104efdf01c3a3c2.png]

questions.question: Triple point can be defined as:

options.text: the condition of temperature under which the gaseous and liquid phases of a substance can exist in equilibrium
the temperature at which solid is converted into liquid
the condition of pressure under which the solid and liquid phases of a substance can exist in equilibrium
the condition of temperature and pressure under which the gaseous, liquid and solid phases of a substance can exist in equilibrium

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is **__the condition of temperature and pressure under which the gaseous, liquid and solid phases of a substance can exist in equilibrium__**. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

 
• The triple point of a substance is the temperature and pressure at which the three phases **(gas, liquid, and solid)** of that substance coexist in thermodynamic equilibrium.
 
• The triple point of water is used to define the Kelvin(K), the base unit of thermodynamic temperature in the International System of Units (SI).
 
• The triple point of water is **273.16K, 0.01° C, or 32.018° F**.
 
 
• **The graph of pressure plotted against temperature the following diagram explains**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f4fece212bc77e370074dc5d77b5e169c5b7672fa5a13ca134b1a94e87d8005e.png] 

If the graph is for water then the three lines shown represent:

(a) the boiling curve (AB) is the locus of points where water and its vapour can exist in equilibrium;

(b) the sublimation curve (AC) is the locus of points where ice and its vapour can exist together in equilibrium;

(c) the solidification curve (AD) is the locus of points where water and ice can exist together.

 
• The triple point is at A where these three lines intersect and where water, water vapour and ice can exist in equilibrium.
 
• The temperature at which this occurs is defined as **273.16 K** on the thermodynamic temperature scale.
 
• The triple point is not exactly at 0° C because under the pressure of its own vapour ice melts at about **0.0075° C**.

questions.question: In which year, the Koya rebellion took place in the eastern Godavari tract?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1879-1880.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

questions.question: ‘Vikramarjuna - Vijaya’ composed by Pampa was written in which of the following languages?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Kannada**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The annals of **Kannada literature** are incomplete without the mention of **Adikavi Pampa**, a revered **poet of the 10th century**.
 
• Known as the first poet of the language, Pampa's works were primarily in Kannada, and he was a firm believer in **Jainism**.
 
• His two epic works, **Vikramarjuna Vijaya or Pampa Bharata and the Adi Purana**, written around **939 CE**, were composed in the champu style and served as court poems for the **Vemulavada Chalukyan king Arikesari II**.
 
• Pampa also held a position as a feudatory under the **Rashtrakuta dynasty king Krishna III**.
 
• His works set the foundation for all subsequent Kannada champu compositions and marked a significant beginning for the **10th century in Kannada literature**, alongside the works of two other **Jain authors, Sri Ponna and Ranna**, collectively known as the **“Three gems of Kannada literature”**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kannada first female poet**

 
 
• **Akka Mahadevi** (circa 1130 – 1160) emerged as a significant figure in** 12th-century Kannada literature **and played a prominent role within the **Lingayat Shaiva sect**.
 
• She is renowned as one of the **pioneering female poets of this era**.
 
 
 
• **Adikavi** (adi ‘primaeval, first’ + kavi ‘poet’) means **‘the first poet**’.

questions.question: Identify an algae that undergoes anisogamous fusion of gametes.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** Eudorina **

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• Algae are chlorophyll-bearing organisms, with a simple **thalloid-like structure** and, are **autotrophic in the mode of nutrition**.
 
• Algae live primarily **aquatic organism**s which may **live in both freshwater and marine water**.
 
• The **algae reproduce by vegetative, asexual, and sexual methods.**
 
• **Sexual reproduction in algae **takes place through the **fusion of two gametes**. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 
• **Isogamous** is a condition in which the fusion of** two gametes takes place which is similar in size**. For example - **Spirogyra, Ulothrix.**
 
• **oogamous** is a condition in which **fusion between one large, nonmotile (static) female gamete and a smaller, motile male gamete occurs**. For example- Volvox.
 
• In **algae, vegetative **reproduction occurs through **fragmentation.** Each fragment develops into a thallus.
 
• In **Asexual reproduction in algae, different types of spores are produced.**

questions.question: Rajya Sabha has to return the money bill to Lok Sabha with or without the recommendation within ________.
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is __**14 Days.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Money Bills**__

 __
 
• Article 110 of the Constitution deals with the definition of money bills.
 
• When a money bill is transmitted to the Rajya Sabha for recommendation and presented to the president for assent, the Speaker endorses it as a **Money bill.**
 
• A money bill can only be introduced in the Lok Sabha and that too on the recommendation of the president.
 
• Every such bill is considered to be a government bill and can be introduced only by a minister.
 
• **After a money bill is passed by the Lok Sabha, it is transmitted to the Rajya Sabha for its consideration**.
 
• The Rajya Sabha has restricted powers about a money bill, It cannot reject or amend a money bill. It can only make recommendations.
 
• It must return the bill to the Lok Sabha within **14 days**, whether with or without recommendations.
 
• The Lok Sabha can either **accept or reject all** or any of the recommendations of the Rajya Sabha.
 
• When a money bill is presented to the president, he may either give his assent to the bill or withhold his assent to the bill but cannot return the bill for reconsideration by the Houses.
 
• **Normally, the president gives his assent to a money bill as it is introduced in Parliament with his prior permission**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• These three together make up the** Parliament- **The President of India, Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha

 
 
• Rajya Sabha is called the Upper house and Lok Sabha is called the Lower House.​
 
• Article 79 defines the constitution of** Parliament**.
 
• **Article 81 is related to Lok Sabha. It is the lower house of the Parliament.**
 
• **Article 83 is related to the duration of the parliament**.
 
• Parliament conducts three sessions in a year namely the **Budget session, Monsoon session, and winter session.**
 
• According to **Article 80 **of the Indian Constitution, out of the 250 members of the Rajya Sabha, 12 are nominated by the President of India.
 
• There was a provision that According to **Article 331** of the Indian Constitution, out of the 552 members of the Lok Sabha.
 
• The President can nominate **2 Anglo Indians** if he/she feels that the community is not being adequately represented in the House, but now it is abolished by the **104th Constitutional Amendment Act.**

questions.question: In North Indian temple architecture, which element denotes the superstructure or tower above the sanctum and the pillared mandapas?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Shikhara.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Shikhara **is a Sanskrit word that means mountain peak. It is the most prominent and visible part of a **Hindu temple of North India**. In South India, it is the same as Vimana.
 
• Shikhara is the rising tower in the Hindu temple architecture of North India.
 
• It is also used in Jain temples.
 
• **Shikhara is over Garbhagriha**. Garbhagriha is the innermost sanctuary of a Hindu and Jain temple where the primary deity of the temple is kept.
 
• Shikhara can be classified into **three main forms - Latina, Sekhar, and Bhumija**.
 
• Shikharas form an element in the many styles of Hindu temple architecture, the three most common styles are the Nagara, the Vesara, and the Dravidian. By at least 600 CE in Odisha, the Latina form of shikhara was well established.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• ** Kalasha**__

 __
 
• The Kalasha is an essential element in Hindu temple architecture.
 
• It is a **pot-shaped structure that crowns the topmost point of the temple.**
 
• Often made of metal or stone, the Kalasha symbolizes purity, abundance, and auspiciousness.
 
• It represents the cosmic axis connecting the earthly and celestial realms.
 
• In North Indian temples, the Kalasha is commonly found atop the Amalaka.
 
 
 
• **Amalaka**__
 __
 
• It is a disc-shaped stone structure positioned at the pinnacle of the temple.
 
• It serves as a **base for the Kalasha****.**__
 
• Commonly seen in North Indian temples, the Amalaka adds architectural elegance.
 
• Its circular form represents the wheel of time or the sun disc.
 
 
 
• __**Antarala (Vestibule)**__
 
 
• The Antarala is a **transitional area connecting the Garbhagriha (sanctum) and the temple’s main hall (Mandapa).**
 
• It acts as a passage for priests and devotees during rituals.
 
• The Antarala often features intricate carvings and decorative elements.
